channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Pope accepts resignation of Denver archbishop, names Colorado Springs bishop as successor
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has accepted the resignation of Archbishop Samuel J. Aquila of Denver and named as his successor Bishop James R. Golka of Colorado Springs, Colo.

item.title: ‘Inexcusable’: Trump account posts, deletes ‘blatantly racist’ depiction of Obamas
item.description: A video posted on President Donald Trump's Truth Social account that depicted former first couple President Barack and Michelle Obama as apes was deleted after widespread outrage denounced the content as racist.

item.title: March for Life rally, national shrine, CUA among infection sites for confirmed measles cases in D.C.
item.description: The March for Life rally, the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception and several buildings at The Catholic University of America were among infection sites for confirmed measles cases in the District of Columbia, the capital city's health department said Feb. 7.

item.title: Vatican confirms pope will not visit U.S. in 2026
item.description: The Vatican press office confirmed that Pope Leo XIV has no plans to visit the U.S. this year.

item.title: In pastoral letter, Archbishop Lori calls for renewed political culture
item.description: In a new pastoral letter released Feb. 9, Archbishop William E. Lori of Baltimore takes the approaching occasion of the nation’s 250th anniversary to address “a moment of grace and responsibility”

item.title: Archbishop Fulton Sheen’s beatification moves ahead after 6-year pause
item.description: Venerable Fulton J. Sheen will soon be beatified, now that the Vatican has given the green light, the Diocese of Peoria, Illinois, announced Feb. 9. No date or location for the beatification was given.

item.title: Radio Interview: Sinners and Saints video series
item.description: Catholic Review Editor Christopher Gunty talks with Tim Jeffries and Joe Reynolds, producers of the popular video series “Sinners and Saints,” which is now filming its third season.

item.title: Who was Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen?
item.description: Once dubbed "God's microphone," Archbishop Sheen announced God's truth in a nonconfrontational, yet no less life-giving, manner to untold millions through radio, print and television.

item.title: With Sheen beatification moving forward, can Church learn from unfortunate episode?
item.description: No matter the obstacles, internally or externally, Sheen's virtue developed and deepened. He grew holier throughout his life, no doubt strengthened by both his own sufferings in the Church and battling his own personal shortcomings, but also on account of habits and practices which nurtured and intensified his faith like the daily holy hour to which he committed as a young priest.

item.title: Archbishop Sheen’s cause for beatification has hit many speed bumps along way
item.description: After decades of anticipation and a cause marked by unexpected delays, the Diocese of Peoria has announced that Venerable Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen -- beloved evangelist, television pioneer and native son of Illinois -- will at last be beatified, a joy-filled announcement that comes only after years of legal disputes and renewed scrutiny briefly slowed his path to the altars.
